correctness.rationale: For V=M2(F_q) with Q=det and nondegenerate polar pairing B in every characteristic, every maximal totally singular 2-plane is in exactly one of the left/right rulings L_i,R_j. Every nonzero rank-one frequency lies in one L_i∩R_j, with q−1 nonzero multiples; invertible frequencies are invisible. Since each D=D^{⊥_B}, a full affine coset-sum view has normal multiplier q² on D and 0 otherwise. Thus nonzero rank-one eigenvalues are q²(w_i+v_j), the constant eigenvalue is q²(Σw_i+Σv_j), and invertible-frequency eigenvalues vanish. For selected positive-direction sets sizes a,c the mean-zero rank-one nullity is (q−1)(q+1−a)(q+1−c), implying injectivity iff a or c equals q+1. Tightness iff one full ruling uniform or both complete with weights constant within each; proper nonempty opposite additions to one full unit-weight ruling yield condition number sqrt(2), full additions restore 1. Constants in inversion follow from eigenvalues on mean and rank-one components. Independently constructed affine-incidence Gram matrices for q=2,3 with four selection patterns and matched full eigenvalue multiplicities; all-q proof is character orthogonality, not extrapolation.

value.rationale: The finite determinant quadric supplies a natural self-dual rank-one frequency cone and two canonical rulings. An exact all-q partial-view tomography classification pinpoints the unique minimal direction architectures, true weighted tightness rigidity and a counterintuitive nonmonotone √2 conditioning penalty from adding only some measurements. These are precise design and inverse-problem invariants, not merely restating Fourier diagonalization.
